note: Attacker-controlled bytes are written to a temporary file and a FILE* is returned.
The FILE* is passed to the vulnerable parser, which reads lines from it.
Initial 1024-byte heap buffer is allocated for reading lines.
line points to the start of the buffer; line_len is 1024.

code: while(((line = fgets(line, line_len, fd)) != NULL) && strlen(line) > 0 && (line[strlen(line) - 1] != '\n'))
note: fgets reads up to 1023 bytes; if no newline is found, the loop continues to grow the buffer.
i is set to the length of the current chunk read by fgets.

code: old_buffer = buffer; old_buffer_len = buffer_len; buffer_len += chunk_len;
note: The old buffer pointer and length are saved before reallocating.
The buffer is grown by 1024 bytes; the old pointer is freed by realloc.

BUG: line is set to &buffer[i] where i is the length of the CURRENT chunk, not the cumulative offset. On the second iteration, i is the length of the second chunk, so line points back near the start of the buffer, overwriting earlier data.
fgets writes into buffer[i..i+1022] where i is the length of the previous chunk. If i is small (e.g., 1), fgets writes near the start of the buffer, corrupting the accumulated line data.

strlen scans from buffer[0] through the corrupted mixed-chunk data. Because chunks overwrite each other, the null terminator may be placed far beyond the logical end, causing strlen to read past the allocated buffer.

A write at buffer[i-1] where i came from the over-read strlen; if i exceeds buffer_len, this is an out-of-bounds write, and the subsequent strlen/read operations trigger the heap-buffer-overflow READ 2.
